rationale: Geometric height fed to atmosisa as if it were geopotential (atmosisa's input is geopotential): a ~13 m shift at 30,000 ft that the exact atmosisa(H) comparison and the published NESC atmosphere must catch.
The range pre-check removed: atmosisa (called with 'action','None') silently holds the boundary value, the clamp VITAL fixed in M1 (FC-106).
The speed cache ignores the altitude key and returns a stale atmosphere for a new altitude.
Aircraft.toRuntime drops a field of the runtime struct, so the object layer no longer hands the core the exact vital.aircraft.f16.config struct.

Wrong DCM convention at the toolbox boundary: C_nb used where Aero.FixedWing.State expects the N->B Euler angles (C_bn, CONVENTIONS 3); the toolbox InertialToBodyMatrix must disagree with VITAL's C_bn.
The toolbox environment built at the geometric height (aircraftEnvironment passes its height to atmosisa, which expects geopotential).

pattern: if isfinite(lo), mLo = (y - lo) / obj.Scale; end
replacement: if isfinite(lo), mLo = (lo - y) / obj.Scale; end
rationale: Sign flip of the lower-bound margin in Rule.evaluate: passes become failures and vice versa, which the M6 engine comparison must catch.

pattern: c = vital.ctrl.pitchSas(AC, env, tr, 'Kq', obj.Kq, 'Ka', obj.Ka, 'Rate', obj.Rate);
replacement: c = vital.ctrl.pitchSas(AC, env, tr, 'Kq', obj.Ka, 'Ka', obj.Kq, 'Rate', obj.Rate);
rationale: The object law passes swapped gains to the functional law (Kq <-> Ka).
